records.source: וּמִקְנֶ֣ה׀רַ֗ב הָיָ֞ה לִבְנֵ֧י רְאוּבֵ֛ן וְלִבְנֵי־גָ֖ד עָצ֣וּם מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּרְא֞וּ אֶת־אֶ֤רֶץ יַעְזֵר֙ וְאֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ גִּלְעָ֔ד וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַמָּק֖וֹם מְק֥וֹם מִקְנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And livestock much belonged to [the] sons of Reuben and to [the] sons of Gad, numerous very; and they saw [the] land of Jazer and [the] land of Gilead, and look, the place [was] a place of livestock.
pieces: The Reubenites and the Gadites owned a great deal of livestock, a very large number of animals. They saw that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead was just the place for livestock.

L.1: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad had much livestock, very numerous; and they saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, and look, the place [was] a place for livestock.

R.1: The tribes of Reuben and Gad owned very large herds and flocks. They looked at the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead and saw that it was a good place for raising animals.

decisions.choice: Jazer and Gilead: grazing land east of the Jordan, newly taken from the Amorites
decisions.reason: Jazer was a town and its district north of the Arnon, captured in 21:32 after the defeat of Sihon (21:21-31). Gilead is the hill country east of the Jordan, with good pasture. Israel was camped on the plains of Moab across from Jericho (22:1), at the edge of this land.

decisions.choice: livestock: herds and flocks, cattle, sheep and goats
decisions.reason: The word covers the animals a family owned and lived from. Much of it may have come from the spoil of Midian (31:32-47). The word opens and closes the verse: the two tribes had much livestock, and the land was a place for livestock.

decisions.choice: look, the place was a place for livestock: what they saw and thought
decisions.reason: The little word that points ("look") turns the story to the tribes' own view: as they looked at the land, they saw that it was exactly what their herds needed. Their request in the next verses grows out of this.

decisions.choice: the Reubenites and the Gadites (Balanced); the tribes of Reuben and Gad (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The sons of Reuben" and "the sons of Gad" are the two tribes, men, women and children. Balanced and Readable name them as groups of people; Literal keeps "the sons of". The same holds through the chapter.

records.heading: Reuben and Gad ask for land east of the Jordan

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ בְנֵֽי־גָ֖ד וּבְנֵ֣י רְאוּבֵ֑ן וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאֶל־אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְאֶל־נְשִׂיאֵ֥י הָעֵדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] sons of Gad and [the] sons of Reuben and said to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and to [the] leaders of the congregation, saying,
pieces: So the Gadites and the Reubenites came and spoke to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the congregation. They said,

L.2: And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben came and said to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the congregation, saying,

R.2: So the Gadites and the Reubenites went to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the community. They said,

decisions.choice: Moses, Eleazar the priest and the leaders: the people's highest authority
decisions.reason: Eleazar had taken his father Aaron's place as priest (20:25-28). With Moses and the tribal leaders he heard the case of Zelophehad's daughters (27:2) and shared out the spoil of Midian (31:13, 26). A request about land went to all of them together.

decisions.choice: Gad and Reuben: from here on Gad is usually named first
decisions.reason: Verse 1 named Reuben first, as the older tribe (1:20, 24). In the rest of the chapter Gad usually comes first (verses 2, 6, 25, 29, 31, 33), perhaps because Gad took the lead in the request; the text does not say why.

records.source: עֲטָר֤וֹת וְדִיבֹן֙ וְיַעְזֵ֣ר וְנִמְרָ֔ה וְחֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וְאֶלְעָלֵ֑ה וּשְׂבָ֥ם וּנְב֖וֹ וּבְעֹֽן׃
records.gloss: Ataroth and Dibon and Jazer and Nimrah and Heshbon and Elealeh and Sebam and Nebo and Beon,
pieces: "Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon,

L.3: "Ataroth and Dibon and Jazer and Nimrah and Heshbon and Elealeh and Sebam and Nebo and Beon,

R.3: "There are the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon.

decisions.choice: nine towns of the land taken from Sihon
decisions.reason: These towns lay in the high plain north of the Arnon, the land Israel took from Sihon king of the Amorites, whose city was Heshbon (21:24-26). The tribes name them as the heart of the land they want. Verses 34-38 tell how they were rebuilt.

decisions.choice: Nimrah, Sebam, Beon: shorter forms of names given in full later
decisions.reason: Nimrah appears to be Beth-nimrah (verse 36), Sebam the Sibmah of verse 38, and Beon probably a short form of Baal-meon (verse 38). The list here gives the names as the tribes speak them.

decisions.choice: There are the towns of ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is a bare list of names that runs on into verse 4. Readable makes it a sentence of its own and says that the names are towns.

records.source: הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לִפְנֵי֙ עֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶ֥רֶץ מִקְנֶ֖ה הִ֑וא וְלַֽעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ מִקְנֶֽה׃ס
records.gloss: the land which struck Yahweh before [the] congregation of Israel, a land of livestock [is] it, and to your servants [is] livestock.
pieces: the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} conquered for the congregation of Israel, is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock."

L.4: the land which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck before the congregation of Israel, it [is] a land for livestock, and your slaves have livestock."

R.4: This land, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} conquered for the community of Israel, is good for raising animals. And we, your servants, have many animals."

decisions.choice: the LORD struck the land before Israel: the victory was the LORD's
decisions.reason: To "strike" a land is to defeat its people. The tribes say that the LORD himself did it, and did it for the whole congregation of Israel (21:24, 34-35), not for two tribes alone. Moses' reply turns on that: the land was won together, and the rest of it must be won together.

decisions.choice: your servants: we, said politely to a superior
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" was the courteous way to address someone of higher rank (Genesis 18:3; 44:18). The tribes mean themselves. The word is the one used for a slave; here it is a form of politeness.

decisions.choice: your slaves (Literal); your servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave" for this word, as it does throughout; Balanced and Readable say "servants", the ordinary polite form. Readable adds "we" so that the reader sees who the servants are.

decisions.choice: conquered
decisions.reason: The verb is "struck". Said of a land, it means the LORD defeated those who held it, so Balanced and Readable say "conquered".

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אִם־מָצָ֤אנוּ חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ יֻתַּ֞ן אֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את לַעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ לַאֲחֻזָּ֑ה אַל־תַּעֲבִרֵ֖נוּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And they said, if we have found favor in your eyes, let be given the land the this to your servants for a possession; do not make us pass over the Jordan.
pieces: "If we have found favor with you," they said, "let this land be given to your servants as their property. Do not make us cross the Jordan."

L.5: And they said, "If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your slaves for a possession; do not make us pass over the Jordan."

R.5: They went on, "If you are pleased with us, please give this land to us, your servants, to own. Do not make us cross the Jordan River."

decisions.choice: if we have found favor in your eyes: a polite way to ask
decisions.reason: The phrase opens a respectful request to someone who can grant or refuse it (Genesis 33:10; 47:29). It shows that the tribes know the decision is not theirs to make.

decisions.choice: a possession: land held as one's own, to keep and pass on
decisions.reason: The word means property that is held and kept in the family. It returns in verses 22, 29 and 32, where the land of Gilead becomes the tribes' possession.

decisions.choice: And they said ... do not make us cross: the request ends with its hardest point
decisions.reason: A second "and they said" begins the request itself after the description of the land, as if after a pause. The last clause, "do not make us cross the Jordan", is what Moses hears as a refusal to join the others in the war (verses 6-7).

decisions.choice: the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" the first time the Jordan is named in the chapter.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה לִבְנֵי־גָ֖ד וְלִבְנֵ֣י רְאוּבֵ֑ן הַאַֽחֵיכֶ֗ם יָבֹ֨אוּ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאַתֶּ֖ם תֵּ֥שְׁבוּ פֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to [the] sons of Gad and to [the] sons of Reuben, [will] your brothers go to the war and you, you will sit here?
pieces: Moses said to the Gadites and the Reubenites, "Are your brothers to go to war while you stay here?

L.6: And Moses said to the sons of Gad and to the sons of Reuben, "Shall your brothers go to the war, and you, you sit here?

R.6: Moses answered the Gadites and the Reubenites, "Will your fellow Israelites go off to war while you stay here?

decisions.choice: your brothers: the other tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow Israelites, the tribes descended from Jacob's other sons (Deuteronomy 3:18). Those who go to war are the fighting men of those tribes.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is a rebuke. The added "you" sets the two tribes sharply against the rest: your brothers fight, and you sit here.

decisions.choice: your fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable says who the brothers are, so that the reader does not think of the men's own brothers.

records.source: וְלָ֣מָּה תְנִיא֔וּן אֶת־לֵ֖ב בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מֵֽעֲבֹר֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And why do you discourage [the] heart of [the] sons of Israel from passing over into the land which has given to them Yahweh?
pieces: Why would you discourage the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from crossing over into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given them?

L.7: And why do you discourage the heart of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from passing over into the land which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given to them?

R.7: Why are you trying to make the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lose heart, so that they will not cross into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given them?

decisions.choice: discourage the heart: hold back their will, so that they do not go
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold back or frustrate. With "heart" it means to take away the courage and will to act. It is used of a father who overrules his daughter's vow (30:6), and again of the spies in verse 9.

decisions.choice: the land the LORD has given them: the gift is already made
decisions.reason: The land across the Jordan is spoken of as already given (13:2; 33:53). Holding back from it would be refusing a gift of the LORD, as the earlier generation did.

decisions.choice: are you trying to make ... lose heart
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the question: the two tribes' request would take away the others' will to go on.

records.source: כֹּ֥ה עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֑ם בְּשָׁלְחִ֥י אֹתָ֛ם מִקָּדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵ֖עַ לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Thus did your fathers when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.
pieces: That is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to look over the land.

L.8: Thus your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.

R.8: Your ancestors did the same thing when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land.

decisions.choice: when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea: the twelve spies
decisions.reason: Moses recalls chapters 13-14: twelve men went to explore Canaan (13:1-3, 17) and came back to the camp at Kadesh (13:26). Kadesh-barnea is the full name of the place (34:4; Deuteronomy 1:19).

decisions.choice: your fathers: the generation before you
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the whole generation that left Egypt, almost all of whom died in the wilderness (14:29-35; 26:64-65).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Readable says "ancestors" for the earlier generation, as in 14:23.

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲל֞וּ עַד־נַ֣חַל אֶשְׁכּ֗וֹל וַיִּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּנִ֕יאוּ אֶת־לֵ֖ב בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְבִלְתִּי־בֹא֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they went up to [the] valley of Eshcol and saw the land, and they discouraged [the] heart of [the] sons of Israel so as not to go into the land which had given to them Yahweh.
pieces: They went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, and then they discouraged the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from entering the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given them.

L.9: And they went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, and they discouraged the heart of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from going into the land which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given to them.

R.9: They went as far as the Eshcol Valley and saw the land. Then they made the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} lose heart, so that they would not go into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given them.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Eshcol: where the spies cut the great cluster of grapes
decisions.reason: The valley was named for the cluster of grapes the spies carried back (13:23-24). They saw how good the land was, and still they turned the people against it (13:27-33).

decisions.choice: they discouraged the heart: the same words as verse 7
decisions.reason: Moses repeats his words from verse 7. The spies' report made the people weep and want to go back to Egypt (14:1-4). He fears the two tribes will do the same.

decisions.choice: the Eshcol Valley
decisions.reason: As in 13:23.

records.source: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh on the day the that, and he swore, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s anger burned on that day, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore this oath:

L.10: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned on that day, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore, saying,

R.10: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became very angry, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made this solemn promise:

decisions.choice: the anger burned: he became very angry
decisions.reason: The word for anger is also the word for the nose, and anger is pictured as heat burning in it. The phrase means fierce anger (11:1, 10; 12:9).

decisions.choice: he swore: the oath of 14:21-23 and 14:28-35
decisions.reason: Moses quotes the oath God swore after the people refused to enter the land: none of that generation but Caleb and Joshua would see it.

decisions.choice: swore this oath (Balanced); made this solemn promise (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces the words of the oath. Balanced and Readable introduce them with a colon.

records.source: אִם־יִרְא֨וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים הָעֹלִ֣ים מִמִּצְרַ֗יִם מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה אֵ֚ת הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֛עְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י לֹא־מִלְא֖וּ אַחֲרָֽי׃
records.gloss: If will see the men who came up from Egypt, from a son of twenty years and upward, the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, because not they have filled after me,
pieces: 'Not one of the men who came up out of Egypt, twenty years old and over, will see the land I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, because they have not followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all their heart,

L.11: 'Surely the men who came up from Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, will not see the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, because they have not fully followed after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},

R.11: 'None of the men twenty years old or older who came out of Egypt will see the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. They have not followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all their heart.

decisions.choice: if they see: surely they will not see
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if" stands for a strong "not", as in 14:23 and 14:30: "if they see" means that they will certainly not see.

decisions.choice: they have not filled after me: they have not followed me fully
decisions.reason: To "fill after" someone is to follow them completely, holding nothing back (14:24). The phrase returns in verse 12 for Caleb and Joshua.

decisions.choice: the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: God promised the land to each of the fathers of Israel (Genesis 12:7; 26:3; 28:13; 50:24). The men counted from twenty years old are the ones listed in the first census (1:3; 14:29).

decisions.choice: swore to give (Balanced); promised (Readable)
decisions.reason: The oath was a promise to give the land, so Balanced adds "to give" and Readable says "promised", as in 14:23.

records.source: בִּלְתִּ֞י כָּלֵ֤ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּה֙ הַקְּנִזִּ֔י וִיהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־נ֑וּן כִּ֥י מִלְא֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, because they have filled after Yahweh.
pieces: except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they have followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all their heart.'

L.12: except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, because they have fully followed after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

R.12: Only Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun will see it, because they have followed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all their heart.'

decisions.choice: the Kenizzite: of the family of Kenaz
decisions.reason: Caleb is called a Kenizzite here and in Joshua 14:6, 14. Kenaz is a name in Edom's family line (Genesis 36:11, 42) and among the peoples of Canaan (Genesis 15:19), so Caleb's family may have joined Israel from outside and become part of Judah (13:6). The text does not explain it further.

decisions.choice: followed the LORD: Moses' quotation of the oath ends in his own words
decisions.reason: In verse 11 God speaks of "me"; here the oath is given as Moses retells it, and he says "the LORD". The two men are those God named in 14:24 and 14:30.

decisions.choice: Only ... will see it
decisions.reason: Readable makes "except" a sentence of its own and repeats "will see it" from verse 11.

records.source: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְנִעֵם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה עַד־תֹּם֙ כָּל־הַדּ֔וֹר הָעֹשֶׂ֥ה הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until was finished all the generation that had done the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s anger burned against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had died out.

L.13: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation that had done the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was finished.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with Israel, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them wander in the desert for forty years. At last the whole generation that had done what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil was gone.

decisions.choice: he made them wander: moved them from place to place with no home
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone stagger or roam about. Israel's years in the wilderness were a sentence that kept them from settling until the guilty generation was gone (14:33-34).

decisions.choice: forty years: counted from the exodus
decisions.reason: The forty years include the time already spent on the way from Egypt. Chapter 14 sets one year for each of the forty days the spies were in the land (14:34).

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of the LORD: did what the LORD judged to be evil
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" someone means in their view or judgment. The evil is measured by the LORD's standard, not by the people's own.

decisions.choice: had died out (Balanced); was gone (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Was finished" means that the whole generation had died; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֣ה קַמְתֶּ֗ם תַּ֚חַת אֲבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם תַּרְבּ֖וּת אֲנָשִׁ֣ים חַטָּאִ֑ים לִסְפּ֣וֹת ע֗וֹד עַ֛ל חֲר֥וֹן אַף־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And look, you have risen up in place of your fathers, an increase of men sinful, to add still to [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh against Israel.
pieces: And now you have taken your fathers' place, a new generation of sinners, to make the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burn against Israel even more!

L.14: And look, you have risen up in place of your fathers, an increase of sinful men, to add still more to the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} against Israel.

R.14: And now you are taking your fathers' place! You are a new crop of sinners, and you will make {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} even angrier with Israel.

decisions.choice: an increase: a new growth, the next generation of the same kind
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root "to increase" and is found only here. It pictures offspring that have sprung up to take the place of the old, and are no better.

decisions.choice: to add still more: the result their refusal would have
decisions.reason: The form can state a purpose or a result. The tribes do not mean to anger the LORD, but Moses says that this is what their request would do.

decisions.choice: the burning of the anger of the LORD: his fierce anger
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, anger is pictured as burning; this form of the word stresses its heat.

decisions.choice: a new generation of sinners (Balanced); a new crop of sinners (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "increase", the root of the word. Balanced says what the increase is, a new generation; Readable keeps the picture of a new growth in plain words.

records.source: כִּ֤י תְשׁוּבֻן֙ מֵֽאַחֲרָ֔יו וְיָסַ֣ף ע֔וֹד לְהַנִּיח֖וֹ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְשִֽׁחַתֶּ֖ם לְכָל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: If you will turn back from after him, and he will add again to leave it in the wilderness, and you will destroy all the people the this.
pieces: If you turn away from following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will once again leave this people in the wilderness, and you will bring ruin on them all."

L.15: If you turn back from after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will again leave it in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people."

R.15: If you turn away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will leave all these people in the desert again, and it will be your fault that they are destroyed."

decisions.choice: turn back from after him: stop following the LORD
decisions.reason: To go "after" someone is to follow them; to turn back "from after" him is to stop following. It is the opposite of the "fully followed" of verses 11-12, the turning back of 14:43.

decisions.choice: leave it: leave the people
decisions.reason: "It" stands for "this people" at the end of the verse, a singular word for the whole nation. The LORD would leave them in the wilderness again, as he did after the spies.

decisions.choice: you will destroy: the two tribes would be to blame
decisions.reason: Moses lays the outcome at their door. A new refusal would bring on the whole people the same judgment as the first, and the fault would be theirs.

decisions.choice: if you turn back: a warning of what would follow
decisions.reason: The small word that opens the verse can mean "for" or "if". Here it sets out a condition and its result: if the tribes turn away, the LORD will leave the people in the wilderness again.

decisions.choice: turn away from the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD where the Hebrew has "him", and says "it will be your fault" for "you will destroy".

records.source: וַיִּגְּשׁ֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ וַ֣יֹּאמְר֔וּ גִּדְרֹ֥ת צֹ֛אן נִבְנֶ֥ה לְמִקְנֵ֖נוּ פֹּ֑ה וְעָרִ֖ים לְטַפֵּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And they drew near to him and said, folds of sheep we will build for our livestock here, and cities for our little ones,
pieces: Then they came up to him and said, "We will build pens here for our livestock and towns for our little ones,

L.16: And they drew near to him and said, "Folds for sheep we will build here for our livestock, and cities for our little ones,

R.16: Then they came up to Moses and said, "We will build pens here for our animals and towns for our children.

decisions.choice: they drew near to him: they come forward with a new offer
decisions.reason: After Moses' rebuke the tribes step closer and make a proposal that answers his charge. The pens are put first in the Hebrew, as the thing on their minds.

decisions.choice: folds for sheep: walled pens for the flocks
decisions.reason: These were enclosures of piled stone where sheep and goats were kept safe at night. The word for the flock covers both sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: little ones: the children, and with them the household that cannot fight
decisions.reason: The word means small children. Here and in verses 17, 24 and 26 it stands for the families left behind; verse 26 adds the wives.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The word for "city" is used of any walled place where people live, however small. Balanced and Readable say "towns"; Literal keeps "cities".

records.heading: An agreement with Reuben and Gad

records.source: וַאֲנַ֜חְנוּ נֵחָלֵ֣ץ חֻשִׁ֗ים לִפְנֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִם־הֲבִֽיאֹנֻ֖ם אֶל־מְקוֹמָ֑ם וְיָשַׁ֤ב טַפֵּ֨נוּ֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הַמִּבְצָ֔ר מִפְּנֵ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And we, we will equip ourselves, hurrying, before [the] sons of Israel, until that we have brought them to their place, and will dwell our little ones in [the] cities of fortification, because of [the] inhabitants of the land.
pieces: But we ourselves will arm for battle and go eagerly ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} until we have brought them to their place. Meanwhile our little ones will live in fortified towns, safe from the people of the land.

L.17: And we, we will equip ourselves, hurrying before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, until we have brought them to their place; and our little ones will dwell in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.

R.17: But we ourselves will take up our weapons and quickly go ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} until we have led them to the land that will be theirs. Meanwhile our children will live in towns with strong walls, to keep them safe from the people who live in this land.

decisions.choice: equip ourselves: arm for war
decisions.reason: The verb means to be equipped and ready for battle. The same word, as verb or as a noun for the armed man, runs through the chapter (verses 20, 21, 27, 29, 30, 32).

decisions.choice: hurrying: going quickly and eagerly
decisions.reason: The text has a word meaning "hurrying", which can describe an eager advance at the head of the army. A word that differs from it by one letter means "in battle formation" (Exodus 13:18; Joshua 1:14; 4:12), and some think it was meant here. The sense is close either way: the tribes promise to go ready for war ahead of the others.

decisions.choice: before the sons of Israel ... to their place: in front of the others, until each tribe has its land
decisions.reason: "Before" here means ahead of, at the front. "Their place" is the land each of the other tribes will receive.

decisions.choice: fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land: protection while the men are away
decisions.reason: With the fighting men across the Jordan, the families would be exposed to the peoples still living around them east of the river. Walled towns would keep them safe.

decisions.choice: to the land that will be theirs
decisions.reason: Readable explains "their place" as the land the other tribes will receive.

records.source: לֹ֥א נָשׁ֖וּב אֶל־בָּתֵּ֑ינוּ עַ֗ד הִתְנַחֵל֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֖ישׁ נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Not we will return to our houses until have taken inheritance [the] sons of Israel, each his inheritance.
pieces: We will not go back to our homes until every one of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} has received an inheritance.

L.18: We will not return to our houses until the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel have inherited, each one his inheritance.

R.18: We will not go back home until all the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have received their share of the land.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a family's share of the land, handed down from one generation to the next
decisions.reason: The noun is land received as a lasting share and passed on in the family (26:52-56; 27:7-11). The verb means to receive one's share. The tribes promise to stay until every share is in hand.

decisions.choice: each his inheritance: every one of them
decisions.reason: "Each" spreads the promise to every tribe and family of Israel. No one will be left without land when the two tribes go home.

decisions.choice: all the other Israelites ... their share of the land
decisions.reason: Readable says that the Israelites meant are the other tribes, and calls the inheritance a share of the land.

records.source: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א נִנְחַל֙ אִתָּ֔ם מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן וָהָ֑לְאָה כִּ֣י בָ֤אָה נַחֲלָתֵ֨נוּ֙ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ מֵעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן מִזְרָֽחָה׃פ
records.gloss: For not we will inherit with them on the other side of the Jordan and beyond, for has come our inheritance to us on the other side of the Jordan eastward.
pieces: We will not take an inheritance with them on the far side of the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on this side of the Jordan, to the east."

L.19: For we will not inherit with them on the other side of the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on the other side of the Jordan, eastward."

R.19: We will not ask for land with them west of the Jordan, because we have already received our share east of the Jordan."

decisions.choice: the other side of the Jordan: first the west, then the east
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used twice for opposite banks. The first time it means the land west of the river, where the other tribes will settle; the second time "eastward" makes plain that it is the speakers' own side, where Israel is camped.

decisions.choice: has come to us: spoken of as already done
decisions.reason: The tribes speak as if the land were already theirs, although Moses has not yet agreed. The words show how settled their wish is.

decisions.choice: the far side ... this side (Balanced); west ... east (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated "other side". Balanced and Readable tell the two banks apart so the reader does not lose track.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה אִֽם־תַּעֲשׂ֖וּן אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה אִם־תֵּחָֽלְצ֛וּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said to them Moses, if you will do the thing the this, if you will equip yourselves before Yahweh for the war,
pieces: Moses answered them, "If you do this, if you arm yourselves for battle before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

L.20: And Moses said to them, "If you will do this thing, if you will equip yourselves before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for the war,

R.20: Moses answered them, "Suppose you do what you have said and arm yourselves to fight before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: before the LORD: in the LORD's presence, as his army
decisions.reason: The war is the LORD's. The ark went before Israel's camp (10:33-35), and the armed men of these tribes later crossed "before the LORD" (Joshua 4:12-13). The phrase comes again and again in verses 20-32.

decisions.choice: if ... if: one long condition across verses 20-22
decisions.reason: Moses sets out each thing the tribes must do (verses 20-22a) before he says what will follow (verse 22b). The condition is the whole war, not only the crossing.

decisions.choice: Suppose you do ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long condition into short sentences, each starting with "Suppose" (verses 20-22), so that the promise in verse 22 still reads as what follows if all this is done.

records.source: וְעָבַ֨ר לָכֶ֧ם כָּל־חָל֛וּץ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה עַ֧ד הוֹרִישׁ֛וֹ אֶת־אֹיְבָ֖יו מִפָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: and will pass over for you every equipped [man] the Jordan before Yahweh until he has dispossessed his enemies from before him,
pieces: and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has driven out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},

L.21: and every equipped [man] of you passes over the Jordan before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has dispossessed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies from before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},

R.21: Suppose all your fighting men cross the Jordan before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has driven out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: until he has dispossessed his enemies: the LORD drives them out
decisions.reason: The one who drives out the enemies is the LORD, and they are "his" enemies (10:35). Israel fights, but the victory is his.

decisions.choice: dispossess: drive out, so that the land passes to another
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession, and with people as its object to dispossess or drive them out (21:32; 33:52-53).

decisions.choice: every armed man (Balanced); all your fighting men (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means one equipped for war; Literal marks the supplied "man". The promise covers every one who can fight, not every person in the tribes.

records.source: וְנִכְבְּשָׁ֨ה הָאָ֜רֶץ לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ וְאַחַ֣ר תָּשֻׁ֔בוּ וִהְיִיתֶ֧ם נְקִיִּ֛ים מֵיְהוָ֖ה וּמִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְ֠הָיְתָה הָאָ֨רֶץ הַזֹּ֥את לָכֶ֛ם לַאֲחֻזָּ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and is subdued the land before Yahweh, and afterward you will return, and you will be free from Yahweh and from Israel, and will be the land the this to you for a possession before Yahweh.
pieces: and the land is brought under control before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then afterward you may return. You will be free of your duty to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to Israel, and this land will be your property before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.22: and the land is subdued before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and afterward you return, then you will be free from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from Israel, and this land will be yours for a possession before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.22: And suppose the land comes under control before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then you may come back home. You will have done what you owe {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and Israel, and this land will be yours before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: subdued: brought under control
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring under, to master (Genesis 1:28). Joshua 18:1 uses it when the land lay subdued before Israel. It does not mean that every enemy was gone.

decisions.choice: free: clear of guilt and of what you owe
decisions.reason: The word means innocent, released from an obligation (Genesis 24:8, 41; Deuteronomy 24:5). Once the war is done, the two tribes will owe nothing more to the LORD or to the other tribes.

decisions.choice: afterward you may return: the first thing that follows when the conditions are met
decisions.reason: After the list of conditions, "afterward you will return" gives the permission to go home, and the promise of the land follows.

decisions.choice: You will have done what you owe
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "free" from the LORD and Israel: their duty will be done.

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֤א תַעֲשׂוּן֙ כֵּ֔ן הִנֵּ֥ה חֲטָאתֶ֖ם לַיהוָ֑ה וּדְעוּ֙ חַטַּאתְכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּמְצָ֖א אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: But if not you will do so, look, you have sinned against Yahweh, and know your sin, that it will find you.
pieces: But if you do not do this, then you will have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and you can be sure that your sin will catch up with you.

L.23: But if you will not do so, look, you have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and know your sin, that it will find you.

R.23: But if you do not do this, you will be sinning against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And you can be sure of this: your sin will catch up with you and bring its punishment.

decisions.choice: look, you have sinned: as good as done
decisions.reason: The pointing word with a past form makes the sin certain: if they hold back, the sin is already done, and done against the LORD, not only against their fellow tribes.

decisions.choice: your sin will find you: the sin will catch up with you and bring its punishment
decisions.reason: Sin is pictured as something that tracks a person down. The word can mean both the wrong done and what it brings on the one who did it (Genesis 4:7; Isaiah 59:12). They cannot escape the result.

decisions.choice: and bring its punishment
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for sin to "find" someone.

records.source: בְּנֽוּ־לָכֶ֤ם עָרִים֙ לְטַפְּכֶ֔ם וּגְדֵרֹ֖ת לְצֹנַאֲכֶ֑ם וְהַיֹּצֵ֥א מִפִּיכֶ֖ם תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃
records.gloss: Build for yourselves cities for your little ones, and folds for your sheep, and what has gone out from your mouth you will do.
pieces: Build towns for your little ones and pens for your flocks, but do what you have promised."

L.24: Build for yourselves cities for your little ones, and folds for your sheep, and what has gone out from your mouth, you will do."

R.24: So go ahead and build towns for your children and pens for your sheep. But be sure to do what you have promised."

decisions.choice: what has gone out from your mouth: what you have promised
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of vows and solemn promises (30:3; Deuteronomy 23:24). Moses holds the tribes to their word as to a vow.

decisions.choice: your little ones ... your sheep: the order of verse 16 turned around
decisions.reason: The tribes spoke of pens for their flocks first and towns for their children second. Moses names the children first.

decisions.choice: So go ahead
decisions.reason: Readable shows that Moses now grants their plan.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בְּנֵי־גָד֙ וּבְנֵ֣י רְאוּבֵ֔ן אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ יַעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י מְצַוֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said [the] sons of Gad and [the] sons of Reuben to Moses, saying, your servants will do as my lord commands.
pieces: The Gadites and the Reubenites said to Moses, "Your servants will do just as my lord commands.

L.25: And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben spoke to Moses, saying, "Your slaves will do as my lord commands.

R.25: The Gadites and the Reubenites answered Moses with one voice, "We, your servants, will do what you, our master, command.

decisions.choice: and said: the two tribes speak as one
decisions.reason: The verb is singular although two tribes are named. They answer with a single voice.

decisions.choice: your servants ... my lord: polite speech to Moses
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, "your servants" means "we". "My lord" is the respectful way to address a superior (11:28; 12:11). They accept Moses' terms in the language of obedience.

decisions.choice: with one voice
decisions.reason: Readable shows what the singular verb conveys.

decisions.choice: your slaves (Literal); your servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

records.source: טַפֵּ֣נוּ נָשֵׁ֔ינוּ מִקְנֵ֖נוּ וְכָל־בְּהֶמְתֵּ֑נוּ יִֽהְיוּ־שָׁ֖ם בְּעָרֵ֥י הַגִּלְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: Our little ones, our wives, our livestock and all our beasts will be there in [the] cities of Gilead,

L.26: Our little ones, our wives, our livestock and all our beasts will be there in the cities of Gilead,

R.26: Our children, our wives, our herds and all our animals will stay in the towns of Gilead.

decisions.choice: livestock and beasts: all the animals together
decisions.reason: The first word is the herds and flocks of verse 1; the second is the general word for animals. Together they mean every animal the tribes own.

decisions.choice: our wives: the whole household stays behind
decisions.reason: Only here are the wives named. The fighting men go; the families and the animals stay in the towns of Gilead, the land the tribes have asked for.

records.source: וַעֲבָדֶ֨יךָ יַֽעַבְר֜וּ כָּל־חֲל֥וּץ צָבָ֛א לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י דֹּבֵֽר׃
records.gloss: and your servants will pass over, every equipped [one] of war, before Yahweh to the battle, as my lord speaks.

L.27: and your slaves will pass over, every [man] equipped for war, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the battle, as my lord says."

R.27: But all of us, your servants, will get ready for war and cross over to fight before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as you, our master, have said."

decisions.choice: equipped for war: armed for military service
decisions.reason: The word for the armed man is joined to the word for an army or military service, the word used in the census for those who can go to war (1:3). The promise covers all the tribes' fighting men.

decisions.choice: as my lord says: they repeat Moses' terms back to him
decisions.reason: The tribes echo verse 25 ("as my lord commands"), and they repeat the very words of Moses: "before the LORD", "to the battle" (verse 20).

decisions.choice: your slaves (Literal); your servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

records.source: וַיְצַ֤ו לָהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵ֚ת אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֑וּן וְאֶת־רָאשֵׁ֛י אֲב֥וֹת הַמַּטּ֖וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And commanded concerning them Moses Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and [the] heads of [the] fathers of the tribes of [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.28: And Moses commanded concerning them Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.28: So Moses gave orders about these tribes to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the family leaders of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: Eleazar and Joshua: those who will carry out the agreement
decisions.reason: Moses will not cross the Jordan himself (20:12; 27:12-14). The priest Eleazar and Joshua, whom he has appointed to lead (27:18-23), will see that the agreement is kept when the land is shared out (34:17).

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers: heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" stands for "house of the fathers", an extended family descended from one ancestor (1:2, 4). Their heads were the family elders of each tribe.

decisions.choice: heads of the ancestral families (Balanced); family leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "heads of the fathers" means; Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

pieces: Moses said to them, "If the Gadites and the Reubenites cross the Jordan with you before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, every man armed for battle, and the land is brought under control before you, then give them the land of Gilead as their property.

L.29: And Moses said to them, "If the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben pass over the Jordan with you, every [man] equipped for the battle before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession.

R.29: Moses told them, "The Gadites and the Reubenites may cross the Jordan with you, every man ready for battle before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. If they do, and the land comes under your control, give them the land of Gilead as their own.

decisions.choice: said to them: to Eleazar, Joshua and the family heads
decisions.reason: "Them" here are the leaders named in verse 28, not the two tribes. Moses gives them the terms they must keep after his death.

decisions.choice: the same terms, now a binding instruction
decisions.reason: Moses repeats the agreement of verses 20-22 in nearly the same words. Said before the leaders, it becomes an order they are bound to carry out (Joshua 1:12-18; 22:1-4).

decisions.choice: ... may cross ... If they do, ...
decisions.reason: Readable puts the condition in two short sentences; it is still a condition, as "If they do" shows.

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֧א יַֽעַבְר֛וּ חֲלוּצִ֖ים אִתְּכֶ֑ם וְנֹֽאחֲז֥וּ בְתֹכְכֶ֖םבְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And if not they will pass over equipped with you, and they will be given possessions in your midst in [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: But if they do not cross over with you armed, they are to receive their property among you in the land of Canaan."

L.30: But if they do not pass over equipped with you, then they shall be given possessions among you in the land of Canaan."

R.30: But if they do not cross over with you ready to fight, they must take their share of land with the rest of you in Canaan."

decisions.choice: they will be given possessions among you: they will have to settle west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made to hold property. If the tribes do not fight, they lose their claim to Gilead and must take land in Canaan with everyone else, where they would have to fight in any case.

decisions.choice: the land of Canaan: the land west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: In Numbers "the land of Canaan" is the land west of the river, whose borders are traced in 34:1-12. Gilead, east of the Jordan, lies outside it.

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲנ֧וּ בְנֵי־גָ֛ד וּבְנֵ֥י רְאוּבֵ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ כֵּ֥ן נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And answered [the] sons of Gad and [the] sons of Reuben, saying, what has spoken Yahweh to your servants, so we will do.
pieces: The Gadites and the Reubenites answered, "Your servants will do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said.

L.31: And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben answered, saying, "What {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken to your slaves, so we will do.

R.31: The Gadites and the Reubenites answered, "We, your servants, will do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said.

decisions.choice: what the LORD has spoken: Moses' terms are the LORD's word
decisions.reason: The tribes speak of Moses' words as spoken by the LORD himself. They accept the agreement as a command of God, not only of Moses.

decisions.choice: your slaves (Literal); your servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

records.source: נַ֣חְנוּ נַעֲבֹ֧ר חֲלוּצִ֛ים לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְאִתָּ֨נוּ֙ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת נַחֲלָתֵ֔נוּ מֵעֵ֖בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: We, we will pass over equipped before Yahweh [into the] land of Canaan, and with us [is the] possession of our inheritance from beyond the Jordan.
pieces: We will cross over armed before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} into the land of Canaan, but the property we inherit will be ours on this side of the Jordan."

L.32: We, we will pass over equipped before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [into] the land of Canaan, and with us [will be] the possession of our inheritance on the other side of the Jordan."

R.32: We will cross over into Canaan ready to fight before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But the land we receive as our share will be east of the Jordan."

decisions.choice: with us the possession of our inheritance: it stays in our hands
decisions.reason: The possession is "with us": the land the tribes will hold as their inheritance remains theirs while they fight. The two words for land held and land inherited are joined (verses 5, 18).

decisions.choice: beyond the Jordan: here the east bank
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, "beyond the Jordan" can name either bank. Here it is the speakers' own side, east of the river.

decisions.choice: this side (Balanced); east (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

records.gloss: And gave to them Moses, to [the] sons of Gad and to [the] sons of Reuben and to [the] half of [the] tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph, [the] kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and [the] kingdom of Og king of the Bashan, the land by its cities with territories, [the] cities of the land all around.
pieces: So Moses gave to the Gadites, the Reubenites and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its towns and their territories, the towns of the whole region.

L.33: And Moses gave to them, to the sons of Gad and to the sons of Reuben and to the half tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of the Bashan, the land by its cities within [their] territories, the cities of the land all around.

R.33: So Moses gave the Gadites, the Reubenites and half of the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdoms of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan. He gave them the whole land, with its towns and the land around them.

decisions.choice: the kingdoms of Sihon and Og: the lands Israel had conquered east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Sihon ruled from Heshbon in the south (21:21-31), and Og ruled Bashan in the north (21:33-35). Their defeat was long remembered (Deuteronomy 2:26-3:11; Psalm 136:19-20).

decisions.choice: the half tribe of Manasseh: named here for the first time
decisions.reason: Half of Manasseh played no part in the request of verses 1-32. Verses 39-42 explain their share: clans of Manasseh had taken land in Gilead and to the north. The other half of the tribe settled west of the Jordan (Joshua 17:1-13).

decisions.choice: the land by its cities with territories: the whole land, town by town, with the country around each
decisions.reason: The phrase is compact. It describes the gift as the land counted out by its towns, each with its surrounding fields and pasture, up to the borders of the whole region.

decisions.choice: king of Bashan
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "the Bashan", a region name that takes the article; Balanced and Readable leave it out, as English does with place names.

records.source: וַיִּבְנ֣וּ בְנֵי־גָ֔ד אֶת־דִּיבֹ֖ן וְאֶת־עֲטָרֹ֑ת וְאֵ֖ת עֲרֹעֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And built [the] sons of Gad Dibon and Ataroth and Aroer,
pieces: The Gadites built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,

L.34: And the sons of Gad built Dibon and Ataroth and Aroer,

R.34: The Gadites rebuilt the towns of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,

decisions.choice: built: rebuilt and fortified towns that already stood
decisions.reason: These towns were there before Israel came: Dibon is named in the song of 21:30. To "build" a town can mean to restore and strengthen it, as the tribes promised in verses 16-17.

decisions.choice: Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer: towns in the south of the land
decisions.reason: Aroer stood on the edge of the Arnon gorge, the southern border (Deuteronomy 2:36; Joshua 13:9, 16). Dibon and Ataroth lay north of it. Joshua 13:9 and 13:16-17 later list Dibon and Aroer within Reuben's land.

decisions.choice: rebuilt the towns of
decisions.reason: Readable says "rebuilt" because the towns already existed, and that the names are towns.

records.source: וְאֶת־עַטְרֹ֥ת שׁוֹפָ֛ן וְאֶת־יַעְזֵ֖ר וְיָגְבֳּהָֽה׃
records.gloss: and Atroth-shophan and Jazer and Jogbehah,
pieces: Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,

L.35: and Atroth-shophan and Jazer and Jogbehah,

decisions.choice: Atroth-shophan and Jogbehah: towns otherwise little known
decisions.reason: Atroth-shophan is a different place from Ataroth (verse 34), though the names are related. Jogbehah lay further north, in Gilead (Judges 8:11).

records.source: וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית נִמְרָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית הָרָ֑ן עָרֵ֥י מִבְצָ֖ר וְגִדְרֹ֥ת צֹֽאן׃
records.gloss: and Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, cities of fortification and folds of sheep.
pieces: Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, as fortified towns, and they built pens for their flocks.

L.36: and Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified cities, and folds for sheep.

R.36: Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran. These were towns with strong walls, and the Gadites also built pens for their sheep.

decisions.choice: fortified cities and folds for sheep: the promise of verses 16-17 kept
decisions.reason: The tribes said they would build pens for their flocks and fortified towns for their families. The list ends by saying they did.

decisions.choice: Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran: towns in the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: Both lay in the valley east of the river, near where Israel was camped (Joshua 13:27). Beth-nimrah is the Nimrah of verse 3.

decisions.choice: they built (Balanced); the Gadites also built (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "folds of sheep" to the list of things built. Balanced and Readable repeat the verb so the pens are not read as more towns.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֤י רְאוּבֵן֙ בָּנ֔וּ אֶת־חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וְאֶת־אֶלְעָלֵ֑א וְאֵ֖ת קִרְיָתָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Reuben built Heshbon and Elealeh and Kiriathaim,
pieces: The Reubenites built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,

L.37: And the sons of Reuben built Heshbon and Elealeh and Kiriathaim,

R.37: The Reubenites rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,

decisions.choice: Heshbon: Sihon's royal city
decisions.reason: Heshbon was the capital of Sihon king of the Amorites (21:26). Elealeh lay close to it, and Kiriathaim is listed with Reuben's towns in Joshua 13:19.

decisions.choice: rebuilt
decisions.reason: As in verse 34.

records.source: וְאֶת־נְב֞וֹ וְאֶת־בַּ֧עַל מְע֛וֹן מֽוּסַבֹּ֥ת שֵׁ֖ם וְאֶת־שִׂבְמָ֑ה וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ בְשֵׁמֹ֔ת אֶת־שְׁמ֥וֹת הֶעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנֽוּ׃
records.gloss: and Nebo and Baal-meon, changed of name, and Sibmah; and they called by names [the] names of the cities which they built.
pieces: Nebo and Baal-meon (their names were changed), and Sibmah. They gave new names to the towns they built.

L.38: and Nebo and Baal-meon, [their] names changed, and Sibmah; and they called by [other] names the names of the cities which they built.

R.38: Nebo, Baal-meon and Sibmah. They changed the names of Nebo and Baal-meon, and they gave new names to the towns they rebuilt.

decisions.choice: changed of name: the names of Nebo and Baal-meon were changed
decisions.reason: Nebo is the name of a Babylonian god, and Baal-meon contains the name of Baal. That may be why the new settlers changed them, though the text does not say. The note may cover only Baal-meon. The old names stayed in use (Isaiah 15:2; Jeremiah 48:22-23).

decisions.choice: they called by names the names of the cities: they renamed the towns
decisions.reason: To call a place by a name is to name it. Giving a town a new name marked it as belonging to its new owners, as in verses 41-42.

decisions.choice: Sibmah: the Sebam of verse 3
decisions.reason: The two spellings name the same town.

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ בְּנֵ֨י מָכִ֧יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֛ה גִּלְעָ֖דָה וַֽיִּלְכְּדֻ֑הָ וַיּ֖וֹרֶשׁ אֶת־הָאֱמֹרִ֥י אֲשֶׁר־בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And went [the] sons of Machir son of Manasseh to Gilead and captured it, and he dispossessed the Amorites who [were] in it.
pieces: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it and drove out the Amorites who lived there.

L.39: And the sons of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it, and he dispossessed the Amorites who [were] in it.

R.39: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it. They drove out the Amorites who lived there.

decisions.choice: Machir son of Manasseh: the leading clan of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Machir was Manasseh's son, and Gilead was Machir's son (26:29; Genesis 50:23). Gilead is both the name of a clan and of the land it settled.

decisions.choice: he dispossessed: Machir as one body
decisions.reason: After the plural "they went" and "they captured", the singular "he dispossessed" treats Machir's descendants as one person, the clan.

decisions.choice: dispossessed: drove out and took their land
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

decisions.choice: the descendants ... drove out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "descendants" for "sons" and use one plural subject for the whole sentence.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־הַגִּלְעָ֔ד לְמָכִ֖יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And gave Moses the Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he dwelt in it.
pieces: So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.

L.40: And Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he dwelt in it.

R.40: So Moses gave Gilead to the clan of Machir son of Manasseh, and they settled there.

decisions.choice: Moses gave Gilead to Machir: the gift is told again later
decisions.reason: Moses' gift of Gilead to Machir is recalled in Deuteronomy 3:15 and Joshua 13:31. "He" who settled there is Machir, the clan.

decisions.choice: the clan of Machir ... they settled
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Machir here is a clan, as in verse 39.

records.source: וְיָאִ֤יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁה֙ הָלַ֔ךְ וַיִּלְכֹּ֖ד אֶת־חַוֺּתֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶתְהֶ֖ן חַוֺּ֥ת יָאִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and called them Havvoth-jair.
pieces: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, went and captured their villages, and he named them Havvoth-jair.

L.41: And Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages, and he called them Havvoth-jair.

R.41: Jair, another descendant of Manasseh, went and captured their villages. He named them Havvoth-jair, which means "villages of Jair."

decisions.choice: son of Manasseh: a descendant of Manasseh
decisions.reason: "Son" often means descendant. Jair came from Manasseh's line through Machir's daughter (1 Chronicles 2:21-22).

decisions.choice: their villages: the villages of the Amorites of Gilead
decisions.reason: "Their" most likely points back to the Amorites of verse 39, whose villages Jair captured.

decisions.choice: Havvoth-jair: "the villages of Jair"
decisions.reason: The name means "Jair's villages" or "Jair's tent villages". It was still in use long after (Deuteronomy 3:14; Joshua 13:30; Judges 10:4).

decisions.choice: a descendant (Balanced); another descendant (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "son" means here; Literal keeps "son". Readable adds the meaning of the name.

records.source: וְנֹ֣בַח הָלַ֔ךְ וַיִּלְכֹּ֥ד אֶת־קְנָ֖ת וְאֶת־בְּנֹתֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֧א לָ֦ה נֹ֖בַח בִּשְׁמֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its daughters, and called it Nobah, by his name.
pieces: And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and he named it Nobah after himself.

L.42: And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its daughters, and he called it Nobah, after his own name.

R.42: Nobah went and captured the town of Kenath and the villages around it. He named it Nobah, after himself.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the villages that belonged to the town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the smaller settlements around it that depended on it (21:25, 32).

decisions.choice: Nobah and Kenath: in the far north of the land east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Nobah is named only here as a man. Kenath lay in the north of the region, near Bashan; 1 Chronicles 2:23 names it with the villages of Jair.

decisions.choice: its villages (Balanced); the villages around it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the town's "daughters" are; Literal keeps the picture.
